Claims are checked against the shipped product and the Help Centre (db/help-articles-2026-10.sql). NO invented statistics. Images live in /images/assistants/<roleKey>/, videos in /videos/assistants/.

social_media_manager.headline: Your social media, planned, written and scheduled — in your voice.
overview: The Social Media Assistant keeps your feeds busy without taking over your week. Tell it how often you want to post and on which days, and it drafts on-brand posts for each platform you connect — captions, hashtags, pictures and short videos — and keeps your review queue stocked ahead of time.

You stay in charge. Every post waits for your approval by default, and you can edit anything before it goes out. When you trust it, you can let a platform publish on its own — and anything the assistant isn't confident about is still held back for you.

steps.title: Connect your accounts
steps.body: Link the platforms you post to: Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X, Threads and YouTube. Instagram needs a professional account (Business or Creator).

steps.title: Set your rhythm
steps.body: Choose how many posts a week, on which days and at what times. The assistant plans around it.

steps.title: Review the drafts
steps.body: Drafts arrive in Review ahead of time. Edit the caption, swap the picture or ask for a rewrite.

steps.title: Approve and relax
steps.body: Approved posts are scheduled to your calendar and published on time.

features.title: Drafts you can see before they post
features.body: Every draft is previewed exactly as it will appear on each platform. Edit the caption, ask for a rewrite, add text on a picture, trim and join video clips or add music, then approve.
features.alt: Three drafted posts previewed as they will look on Instagram, LinkedIn and X

features.title: A review queue that is never empty
features.body: The assistant drafts ahead of your schedule, so there is always a week of posts waiting for a quick yes, a tweak or a no with a reason it learns from.

features.title: Everything on one calendar
features.body: See what is scheduled, published and waiting across every platform. Drag a post to move it.
features.alt: A month of scheduled and published posts on the calendar

features.title: Pictures without the hassle
features.body: Upload your own, choose a free stock photo or video, use a branded graphic in your colours, or generate an image with AI. Your library is shared by all your assistants.

faqs.q: Will it post without asking me?
faqs.a: Not unless you switch that on for a platform. By default every draft waits for your approval. Even when publishing without review is on, posts appear on your calendar first and anything the assistant isn't confident about is held for you.

faqs.q: How does it learn my style?
faqs.a: From your setup answers — your brand voice, topics and rules — and from the reasons you give when you reject or edit a draft. It turns your corrections into rules it follows next time.

faqs.q: Does it use tasks?
faqs.a: Each drafted post uses one task, however many platforms it goes to. An AI image adds 1 task, an AI video 20 (on the Busywork Buster plan) and an AI music track 20 (12 if you share it with the Be More Swan community). A post to X with a link uses 10. Your own uploads, stock media and branded graphics are free.

faqs.q: Which platforms can it post to?
faqs.a: Facebook Pages, Instagram, LinkedIn (your personal feed), X, Threads and YouTube. Instagram must be a professional account (Business or Creator) linked to a Facebook Page, because personal Instagram accounts cannot be used. TikTok and LinkedIn Company Pages are coming soon.

blog_writer.headline: Long-form articles in your voice, on a schedule — published on your own site.
overview: The Blog Writing Assistant researches and writes articles about the topics your customers search for, in your tone, on a cadence you choose. Each draft lands in your review queue and opens in Blog Studio, where you can edit it like a document.

Approved articles are scheduled into the next free slot and appear on your own website through a simple embed, on LinkedIn as articles, and on the Swan Index if you choose. Connect Google Search Console and it tells you which posts are winning — and which need a refresh.
highlights: Spots posts that need a refresh

steps.title: Tell it what to cover
steps.body: Topics, tone and how often you want to publish.

steps.title: Review each draft
steps.body: Drafts arrive in Review. Open one in Blog Studio to edit, add pictures or ask for changes.

steps.title: Approve it
steps.body: It is scheduled into your next free slot — you never have to pick a date.

steps.title: It appears on your site
steps.body: Paste one embed snippet into your website once, and every approved article shows up there, styled to match.

features.title: Real articles, published on a real blog
features.body: Every article on the Be More Swan blog was researched, drafted and scheduled by our own Blog Writing Assistant, then approved by a person. Yours works the same way — and you edit drafts in Blog Studio, a full editor with headings, pictures and columns.
features.alt: The Be More Swan blog — written by its own Blog Writing Assistant

features.title: Your blog, on your website
features.body: A drop-in embed renders your articles on a page of your own site, with a permanent shareable link for every post.
features.alt: A published article, with its AI-assistance note

features.title: Search performance that tells you what to do
features.body: Connect Google Search Console to see impressions and clicks for each post. When a post's traffic starts to slide, the assistant flags it for a refresh.

faqs.q: Do I need a blog already?
faqs.a: No. The embed puts your blog on any page of your website, and every post also gets its own shareable link.

faqs.q: Can I write some posts myself?
faqs.a: Yes. Press New blog post, give it a subject, and either write it yourself or ask the assistant to draft it for you.

faqs.q: Does it use tasks?
faqs.a: Each drafted article uses one task, and an AI image adds 1 more. Stock pictures and your own uploads are free.

newsletter_editor.headline: Newsletters and email flows your audience actually opens.
overview: The Email Marketing Assistant writes your newsletters and email flows, and helps you grow the list they go to. Ask it to draft an email, plan a welcome series, or turn your latest blog post into a newsletter — then edit it in Email Studio and approve it.

Your Audience is built in: sign-up forms for your website, imports, segments and tags, and customers your Lead Generation Assistant has won. Only people who have agreed to hear from you are emailed, and anyone who unsubscribes is never emailed again.

steps.title: Bring your audience
steps.body: Import a list, add a sign-up form to your website, or add customers as you win them.

steps.title: Ask for an email
steps.body: Describe what you want to say. The assistant drafts it in your voice, with a subject line and preview text.

steps.title: Edit and preview
steps.body: Adjust the words and layout in Email Studio and see exactly how it will look.

steps.title: Approve and send
steps.body: Choose who it goes to — everyone, or a segment — and send it now or schedule it.

features.title: Email Studio
features.body: Write, design and preview emails in one place. Ask the assistant to draft, shorten, or suggest a better subject line.
features.alt: Email Studio with a newsletter draft open

features.title: An audience you can work with
features.body: Search, filter and group your contacts, build segments that keep themselves up to date, and export to Excel whenever you need to.
features.alt: The Audience page with segments, tags and contacts

features.title: Campaigns that run themselves
features.body: Describe a sequence — a welcome series, for example — and the assistant plans and drafts every email. It can start automatically when someone signs up through one of your forms.

faqs.q: Who can it send to?
faqs.a: Only people in your Audience who can be emailed: people who signed up, people you imported with their permission, and customers you chose to add. Every email carries an unsubscribe link.

faqs.q: Can I send from my own domain?
faqs.a: Yes. Set up a sending domain and your emails come from your own address, which helps them land in the inbox.

faqs.q: Does it use tasks?
faqs.a: Each email it drafts or rewrites uses one task. Sending doesn't.

lead_qualifier.headline: New customers found, researched and contacted — with your approval.
overview: The Lead Generation Assistant finds businesses that match your ideal customer, scores each one against what you told it, finds their published contact details and drafts a personal email for each good fit.

You review every email before it is sent, from your own Gmail or Outlook. Replies come back into the assistant, follow-ups are sent for you if you want them, and when a deal is won you can add the new customer to your Audience in one click.

steps.title: Describe who you want
steps.body: In plain English — for example, independent cafés in Leeds with no online ordering.

steps.title: Approve the search plan
steps.body: See the searches it will run before it spends anything, and edit them if you like.

steps.title: Review the leads
steps.body: Each company is scored hot, warm or cold with the reasons, and the good ones get a drafted email.

steps.title: Approve the outreach
steps.body: Read each email and approve it. It's sent from your address, and replies come back to you.

features.title: Every lead, explained
features.body: See why each company scored the way it did, with links to the pages the assistant read. Research a company further, correct its details, or move it on to outreach.
features.alt: Leads scored hot, warm or cold, each with a suggested next step

features.title: Personal outreach, not mail merge
features.body: Each email is written for that company, in your sales tone, and waits for your approval. Approving is what sends.
features.alt: A personal outreach email drafted for one café, waiting for approval

features.title: Conversations and outcomes in one place
features.body: Replies, follow-ups and your answers sit in one thread per lead. Record the outcome — won, lost or not a fit — and see what is working.

faqs.q: Will it email people without asking me?
faqs.a: No. Every outreach email waits for your approval — approving is what sends it. If you've chosen to chase leads who don't reply, approving also schedules up to three follow-ups, which stop as soon as they reply or you record an outcome.

faqs.q: Why don't all leads have an email address?
faqs.a: It only uses contact details it can find for that business — roughly one small business in three has a findable address. You can add one yourself with Edit, or ask it to look again later.

faqs.q: What do I need before sending?
faqs.a: Your business postal address, which the law requires in every marketing email, and ideally a connected Gmail or Outlook mailbox. Without one, you get each draft to send yourself.

faqs.q: Does it use tasks?
faqs.a: Each finished search uses one task, however many leads it finds.

campaign_orchestrator.headline: One objective. Every assistant pulling the same way.
overview: The Marketing Campaign Orchestrator turns a single goal — fifty new leads by March, a product launch, a busy season — into coordinated work for your other assistants. It plans the campaign, writes briefs for each assistant, and tracks what comes back.

Every piece of work still comes to you for approval, and you decide how much of your monthly allowance a campaign may use. It explains each decision it wants to make, with the evidence behind it, before acting.

steps.title: Set an objective
steps.body: What the campaign is for, who it is aimed at, and what counts as success.

steps.title: Approve the plan
steps.body: It proposes which assistant does what, and what it will cost in tasks.

steps.title: Your assistants get to work
steps.body: Posts, articles, emails and lead searches are commissioned, and each comes back to you for approval.

steps.title: Watch it land
steps.body: Progress against your target, what was spent and what worked — kept for the next campaign.

features.title: A plan you can read
features.body: Every order to another assistant shows what was asked, what it cost and what came back.
features.alt: Two running campaigns with progress against their targets and task budgets

features.title: Decisions with the evidence attached
features.body: When it wants to change course, it says why, shows the evidence and tells you what happens if you do nothing. Nothing changes until you approve.

features.title: Lessons that carry forward
features.body: What each campaign learned is kept and read when the next one is planned, so you never start from scratch.

faqs.q: Do I need other assistants first?
faqs.a: Yes — it works by briefing them. Hire the assistants you want it to coordinate, then set an objective.

faqs.q: Can it overspend?
faqs.a: No. You set how much of your monthly task allowance a campaign may use, and it asks before going further.

brand_designer.headline: Tell it what you need a picture or video for. Pick the one you like.
overview: The Brand Designer finds stock photos and videos, makes AI images and videos, designs simple graphics in your brand colours with your logo, and lays out printable flyers — then shows you the options side by side.
Pick the ones you like and they are saved to your library, ready for every assistant to use. Nothing is used until you approve it, and you can bring in your own files and Canva designs too.

steps.title: Say what it's for
steps.body: A launch post, a blog header, an email banner — describe the picture or video you need.

steps.title: See the options
steps.body: Stock photos and videos, AI images and branded graphics, side by side.

steps.title: Pick the one you like
steps.body: Approve it, or turn options down with a reason and get a fresh round.

steps.title: Use it everywhere
steps.body: Approved pictures land in your library for every assistant to use.

features.title: Options from every source
features.body: Free stock photos and videos, branded graphics in your own colours and font, and AI images or video when you want something unique.
features.alt: A brief with four branded options to choose from

features.title: Your brand rules, followed
features.body: Set your photo style, what to include and what never to show. Every AI picture follows them.

features.title: Bring your own
features.body: Add your own uploads and Canva designs as options alongside what the designer finds.

faqs.q: Does it use tasks?
faqs.a: Stock photos, stock videos and branded graphics are free. AI images use 1 task for a round of four, having it write a flyer's words uses 1 task, and an AI video clip uses 20 tasks — AI video is on the Busywork Buster plan.

faqs.q: Can I use my own photos?
faqs.a: Yes — upload them, or import designs from Canva, and they appear as options alongside the rest.

faqs.q: Can it make a flyer I can print?
faqs.a: Yes. Say what the flyer is for and pick a paper size — A4, A5, A6 or DL. It writes the words, or you type your own, and lays them out up to three ways in your colours. Approve one and you get a PDF to print at home, and one with bleed for a print shop.

video_producer.headline: Say what the video is about. Check the storyboard. Get a finished video.
overview: The Video Producer makes short videos, vertical, square or wide. It writes the script from your business details and products, picks stock footage, your own pictures or clips, branded cards or AI scenes, and adds a voiceover and captions. Read the voiceover yourself if you prefer, line by line. Give it your own footage, or film yourself on the Videos tab, and it says what it sees, suggests edits and cuts out pauses and “um”s.

You check the storyboard scene by scene before anything is made, and choose where the words on each scene sit and how loud the music is. The finished video is saved to My Content: download it, or use it with any of your assistants. The Video Producer never posts anything itself.

steps.title: Say what it should say
steps.body: A sentence or two — an offer, a product, a tip — or your own footage. Pick the length, voice and shape.

steps.title: Check the storyboard
steps.body: Every scene with its voiceover line and words on screen. Change any scene, or ask for a new plan with your notes.

steps.title: Make the video
steps.body: It shows what it will use before you press it, then voices, captions and edits the video.

steps.title: Use it
steps.body: Play it, download it, or use it from My Content. Change it later and you get a new version.

features.title: Your products, your pictures
features.body: Product scenes use your own photos — it never uses AI to picture what you sell. AI scenes never have words painted into them.
features.alt: A Video Producer storyboard: each scene with its voiceover line, words on screen and where its picture comes from

features.title: Voiceover and captions included
features.body: Six voices to choose from. Captions show each word as it’s spoken, so the video works with the sound off.

features.title: Videos from your posts and campaigns
features.body: Turn a post into a video version with one click and it goes back onto that post, have it plan up to three storyboards a week, or let your Campaign Assistant commission one.

faqs.q: Does it use tasks?
faqs.a: Planning a storyboard is free. Making the video uses tasks only for AI scenes and the voiceover: 20 tasks for an AI clip (at most 3 in a video), 1 for an AI picture and 1 for the voiceover. Stock footage, stock photos, your own pictures and branded cards use none. Making videos is on the Busywork Buster plan.

faqs.q: Can it edit my own footage?
faqs.a: Yes. Give it videos you filmed (up to 5 minutes each) and it says what it sees, suggests edits you tick or untick, and cuts out pauses, “um”s and repeated takes. Your videos are never changed — the edits go into the new video. Reviewing a video it hasn’t seen before uses 2 tasks.

faqs.q: Does it post my videos?
faqs.a: No. It saves the finished video to My Content. Download it for anywhere, including TikTok, or pick it from My Content in any of your assistants.

mystery_shopper.headline: See your website through a stranger's eyes, and fix what's costing you sales.
overview: The Mystery Shopper reads your homepage the way real buyers do: a sceptical first-time visitor, a buyer comparing you with up to three competitors, and an AI assistant deciding whether it could recommend you. It scores your page out of 100 and tells you the changes that matter most.
Every suggested rewrite quotes your page word for word. It checks your site again every week, confirms each change went live, and tells you when a competitor changes their headline, prices or offer.

Your site is hosted with Be More Swan and you have the Website Assistant too? Hand it any change. It shows you exactly what it will change, nothing is saved until you approve it, and once you publish, the Mystery Shopper checks the change is live.
highlights: Reads your site like a buyer
Side by side with your competitors
Fixes made with your Website Assistant, then checked

steps.title: Give it your website
steps.body: Your homepage, who it's for, what visitors should do, and up to three competitors.

steps.title: Get your score
steps.body: A score out of 100 across first impression, competitors and AI search readiness.

steps.title: Make the top changes
steps.body: The highest-impact fixes, each with what your page says now and what to say instead. Make them yourself, or hand them to your Website Assistant.

steps.title: It checks every week
steps.body: The next check confirms each change is live and spots what your competitors changed.

features.title: A score you can trust
features.body: Strict, repeatable checks: an unchanged page keeps exactly the same score, and you can see every check your page is missing.
features.alt: A website scored 71 out of 100 across first impression, competitors and AI search readiness

features.title: The wording, already written
features.body: Each fix shows what your page says now and what to try instead, with [placeholders] wherever it needs a fact only you know.
features.alt: Suggested fixes, each with the current wording and a suggested replacement

features.title: Your eyes on the market
features.body: Every week it compares you with up to three competitors, tells you when one changes their headline, prices or offer, and lines up briefs for your other assistants.
features.alt: A competitor's new headline and prices, with briefs ready for the Social Media and Blog Writing Assistants

features.title: Ready for AI search
features.body: It checks how an AI assistant is likely to read your page — whether it can tell what you do, who you serve and what to quote — so you are easier to recommend.

faqs.q: Does it change my website?
faqs.a: Not by itself. It reads your site and writes the changes. If your site is hosted with Be More Swan and you have the Website Assistant, you can hand a change to it: it shows you exactly what it will change, and nothing is saved until you approve it and publish. Otherwise you, or whoever runs your site, make them. Either way, the Mystery Shopper checks each change is live.

faqs.q: Does it use tasks?
faqs.a: A check that re-scores your site uses 1 task from your monthly allowance. A week where nothing on your site or your competitors' sites changed costs nothing.

faqs.q: Does it ask ChatGPT about my business?
faqs.a: No. The AI search part of the score simulates how an AI assistant is likely to read your page. It does not query ChatGPT or any other assistant.

faqs.q: What can't it see?
faqs.a: Only public pages are read. It never logs in, fills in forms or buys anything, and it respects sites that ask crawlers to stay out. If your homepage shows text only after JavaScript runs, it tells you — that is often what AI crawlers see too.

faqs.q: Can I try it first?
faqs.a: Yes. The free website check on this page gives you a first-impression score and the one change to make first, in about 30 seconds.

website_assistant.headline: Describe your website. Approve it. Done.
overview: The Website Assistant writes your website from what it already knows about your business: your profile, your products, your brand kit and the answers you give when you set it up. Ask for a whole site and it drafts every page; ask in chat for a change and it shows you exactly what it will do before anything is saved.

It never makes things up. Where a page needs a fact only you know, such as a price, a customer quote or how long you have been trading, it leaves a clear [placeholder] for you to fill in. You see every page in a live preview, on a desktop or a phone, as you work.

Your site can do more than tell people about you. Add a shop with checkout on your own Stripe account, bookings for appointments, classes and events, contact and sign-up forms, and your customer reviews. With the Blog Assistant, your articles appear on your site at /blog, and with the Mystery Shopper, the changes it suggests come straight to the Website Assistant for you to approve.

steps.title: Tell it about your site
steps.body: What visitors should do, the pages you want, and how it should feel.

steps.title: Get a first draft
steps.body: Every page written from your business details, products and brand kit.

steps.title: Fill in the gaps
steps.body: Replace each [placeholder] with a fact only you know, and edit anything you like.

steps.title: Ask for changes
steps.body: Tell it in chat what to change; it shows you the change before you approve it.

features.title: Your whole site, drafted
features.body: Pages, headings, wording, questions buyers ask and a clear next step on every page, written in plain British English.
features.alt: The website editor listing its pages, beside a live preview of the home page

features.title: Edit anything, see it straight away
features.body: Change a heading, a button or a whole section and the preview shows it the moment you save. Links to your own pages are checked against the pages you have, so none lead nowhere.
features.alt: Editing the opening section of a home page, with the preview beside it

features.title: On brand, and readable
features.body: It starts from your brand kit, and it refuses colour choices that would make the text hard to read. Check every page on a phone before anyone else sees it.
features.alt: The design settings beside a phone-sized preview of the site

features.title: Ready for search
features.body: Every page gets its own search title and description, one main heading, a sitemap and the details search engines use to understand your business.

features.title: Sell, take bookings and hear from customers
features.body: Sell your products with checkout on your own Stripe account; we take no cut. Take bookings for appointments, classes and events, with deposits, day-before reminders, a change-or-cancel link and sync with your Google or Outlook calendar. Contact and sign-up forms send enquiries to your email and sign-ups to your mailing list.

features.title: Reviews, your blog, and a second pair of eyes
features.body: Show your customer reviews and ask each customer for one after a booking or order. With the Blog Assistant, its articles appear on your site at /blog. With the Mystery Shopper, the changes it suggests come to the Website Assistant, which makes them once you approve.

faqs.q: Can I put my site live?
faqs.a: Yes. Press Publish and your site goes live on its own free address, yourname.bemoreswan.site, or on a domain you own. Until you publish, it stays a private draft that search engines are told to ignore. You can publish changes, go back to an earlier version or take the site offline at any time.

faqs.q: Does it use tasks?
faqs.a: Drafting your whole site, importing your current site, or having it place your own words on a page each uses 1 task from your monthly allowance (an import only uses one if a draft is made). Editing pages yourself, and approving changes it suggests in chat, costs nothing.

faqs.q: I already have a website. Can I bring it over?
faqs.a: Yes, if it is your own. Give it the address of your current site, whether it is on Wix, Squarespace, WordPress, Shopify, Webflow or built for you, and it reads your home page and up to 20 pages from its menu into a draft. Your words are kept exactly as they are, and your links, buttons, menu, pictures and social profiles come across too, with your colours and fonts set as your design. Posts from your old blog arrive as drafts in your Blog Assistant, and products from an old shop can be added to your Products & Services with a tick. Prices are never put on your pages, because they belong with your products. You see the imported draft beside your current one and choose whether to use it, and nothing goes live until you publish.

faqs.q: How many pages can I have?
faqs.a: As many as your site needs. No plan limits how many pages your website has.

faqs.q: Can I sell online or take bookings?
faqs.a: Yes. Add a shop, with checkout on your own Stripe account and no cut taken by us (Stripe's card fees apply), and bookings for appointments, classes and events, with deposits, reminders and sync with your Google or Outlook calendar. Prices and services come from your Business Information, so they are never made up.

faqs.q: Can my blog be on my website?
faqs.a: Yes. If you have the Blog Assistant, the articles you approve appear on your site at /blog, with their own page each.

faqs.q: Can it make the changes the Mystery Shopper suggests?
faqs.a: Yes, if your site is hosted with Be More Swan and you have both assistants. Hand a suggested change to the Website Assistant and it shows you exactly what it will change. Nothing is saved until you approve it, and after you publish, the Mystery Shopper checks the change is live.

faqs.q: Will it make up reviews or prices?
faqs.a: No. It only states what is in your business details and products. Anything else, such as a customer quote or a number, is left as a [placeholder] for you to fill in.

faqs.q: Do I need to know how to build a website?
faqs.a: No. There is no code and no drag-and-drop. You describe what you want, or edit the words directly, and the layout is handled for you.
